::: {.callout-important title="Before you start"}
Complete the [one-time setup](objectives.qmd#one-time-setup) so that

Unless stated otherwise, every command below runs from
`labs/greeting-capsule/` inside your local clone.

## Step 1 — Fetch the upstream artefacts

Run the fetch script to download the normative schema and the three
fixtures used by this walkthrough at the pinned upstream commit:

```bash
bash solution/fetch-upstream.sh
```

Expected output:

```
fetch-upstream: downloaded upstream artefacts at bf071c2c1b57 into .../labs/greeting-capsule/build/upstream
```

The `build/upstream/` directory it creates sits under the lab-local
`build/` directory (ignored in the lab's `.gitignore`) and is **not**
committed. The lab reads these files; it does not copy them into the
Academy tree. `build/` is also one of the pruned directory names in
`scripts/oels_ci_validate.py`, so the fetched OE-shaped fixtures do
not trigger `UnknownDefinition` diagnostics under `--fail-on-gap`.

## Step 2 — Write the capsule document

Author the capsule verbatim from memo1 §3 (identifier conformed to
memo2 §3 D3 as `oe.greeting`). Create `solution/capsule.yaml` with:

```yaml
apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1
kind: Capsule
metadata:
  name: greeting
  version: 0.1.0
spec:
  capability: oe.greeting
  inputs:
    value:
      type: string
      required: true
  outputs:
    greeting:
      type: string
  dependencies: []
```

This is the smallest capsule document that satisfies memo1 §1
(required field set) and memo2 §3 D3 (capability identifier grammar).

## Step 3 — Validate it against the upstream schema

Run the one-liner JSON Schema validation:

```bash
python3 -c 'import json, yaml, jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(yaml.safe_load(open("solution/capsule.yaml")), json.load(open("build/upstream/capsule.schema.json"))); print("valid")'
```

Expected output: `valid`.

Now show the schema rejects one upstream invalid fixture for the
stated reason. The traceback below is piped through
`grep ValidationError` so the expected output stays a single line
(the full traceback also dumps the schema and failing instance; the
grep extracts just the diagnostic line):

```bash
python3 -c 'import json, yaml, jsonschema; jsonschema.validate(yaml.safe_load(open("build/upstream/fixtures/invalid/missing-outputs.yaml")), json.load(open("build/upstream/capsule.schema.json")))' 2>&1 | grep ValidationError
```

Expected output:

```
jsonschema.exceptions.ValidationError: 'outputs' is a required property
```

The upstream fixture carries a top-of-file comment
`# fails: memo1 §1 — spec.outputs is required (may be {} but must be present).`
— matching the schema message.

## Step 4 — Implement the capability

::: {.callout-important title="Python call convention is a course-local teaching harness"}
The function-call shape used below is a **course-local teaching
harness only**. The implementation convention for capsules belongs
to `open-engineering-capsule/source`, which has published none yet
(`memo24` §2.1 as updated by observation at `bf071c2c1b57`). When
that convention is published the Academy will consume it; this lab
will not fork or shadow it.
:::

Create `solution/greeting.py` with a single function behind the
declared `spec.inputs`/`spec.outputs` of the capsule. The function
reads `value` (declared required, type `string`) and returns
`greeting` (declared type `string`). A missing required input raises
a structured `MissingRequiredInput` error (memo23 §5 rule 9 "graceful
failure").

See [`solution/greeting.py`](solution/greeting.py) for the full
implementation.

## Step 5 — Run the tests

Two test modules live under `solution/tests/`:

- `test_greeting.py` — unit tests for `greeting()`;
- `test_contract.py` — reads `solution/capsule.yaml` and asserts the
  implementation honours each declared input/output name and type,
  plus the structured error on each declared-required input.

Run them with:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s solution/tests
```

Expected tail of output:

```
Ran 8 tests in 0.001s

OK
```

## Step 6 — Compose a minimal Pico and validate it

Create `solution/pico.yaml` per memo1 §3, declaring the capability
need with a caret pin:

```yaml
apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1
kind: Pico
metadata:
  name: hello-pico
spec:
  type: greeter
  capabilities:
    - oe.greeting@0.1.0
  implementation: {}
  state: {}
  events: {}
```

Validate the Pico against the Academy's `definitions/pico.yaml` by
extracting its `spec.schema` and running JSON Schema 2020-12
validation (this is the only Pico-shaped contract the repository
offers today; no dedicated Pico validator CLI exists, so no new
validator is added here):

```bash
python3 -c 'import yaml, jsonschema; defn = yaml.safe_load(open("../../definitions/pico.yaml")); jsonschema.validate(yaml.safe_load(open("solution/pico.yaml")), defn["spec"]["schema"]); print("valid")'
```

Expected output: `valid`.

## Step 7 — Resolve the capability by hand

No reference validator / resolver exists yet — memo2 §5 follow-up (b)
is pending. For this lab you therefore resolve
`spec.capabilities: [oe.greeting@0.1.0]` against the one installed
provider (`solution/capsule.yaml`) by hand, applying memo2 §2 D2
(SemVer / caret / `0.x`) and memo2 §3 D3 (grammar) step by step.
Record the result in `solution/resolution.md`, in the shape of
upstream `fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml` — see
[`solution/resolution.md`](solution/resolution.md) for the finished
report. Compare the `outcome`/`resolution` block in your file against
the upstream scenario: it should be byte-equivalent.

## Troubleshooting

::: {.callout-warning title="Heads up"}
- If `fetch-upstream.sh` prints `failed to retrieve …`, the private
  upstream repository likely requires authentication. Install the
  GitHub CLI and run `gh auth login`; the script then falls back to
  `gh api` automatically.
- If the Step 3 validation fails with a different message, re-copy
  the capsule block verbatim from Step 2 — a missing colon or an
  extra indent changes the shape.
- If `python3 -m unittest` reports `ModuleNotFoundError: No module
  named 'yaml'` or `'jsonschema'`, re-run `python3 -m pip install
  --user jsonschema pyyaml` from [one-time setup](objectives.qmd#one-time-setup).
- The fetched upstream files land under `build/upstream/`, not
  `upstream/`. `build/` is in `scripts/oels_ci_validate.py`'s pruned
  directory list, so after Step 1 the repository's OELS gate
  (`python3 scripts/oels_ci_validate.py --fail-on-gap`) still ignores
  them and no extra `UnknownDefinition` diagnostics appear.
:::
